subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence.

After much of efforts, I could finally __hit the nail on the head__ and succeed.
solution:
The correct answer is **'option 2.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hit the nail on the head:** say or do exactly the right thing (कुशलता से कार्य करना) 

 
 
• **Example: ** The detective's deduction hit the nail on the head, leading them to the culprit.
 
 
 
• **Speak or act precisely:** Something done with complete accuracy or perfection. (बिल्कुल सटीक)
 
 
• **Example:** We perform speech acts when we offer an apology.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct idiom is** 'speak or act precisely.**

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Option B.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Accidentally injure oneself **(गलती से खुद को घायल करना): This option is incorrect because "hit the nail on the head" does not imply injuring oneself.
 
• **Make an error** (गलती करना): This option is incorrect because "hit the nail on the head" suggests doing something correctly, not making a mistake.
 
• **Complete a task swiftly** (तेजी से कार्य पूरा करना): While "hit the nail on the head" can imply success, it doesn't necessarily mean swiftness. It focuses more on doing something precisely.

78:Td10,
The correct answer is '**everything turn out**'.</s
